scope: CDS exterior public ground floor and approach; no interior, footprint, tower, podium, or collision-envelope change

primarySources.evidence: Ground landscape plan establishes a paved public edge around the western tower and eastern podium. It is a planning presentation, not an as-built door or threshold survey.

Architect discussion describes the transparent public and collaborative spaces addressing the street and the eastern arrival stair. Supports an articulated glazed ground edge rather than the former blank dark box.
Project identity and completed building context. Not used as a measured entrance plan.

existingModelRetained.foundation: Rigid building base from buElevation(anchor); new paving uses the shared bare-earth DEM without changing it
existingModelRetained.groundEnvelope: Existing two blocks, including concave union and both collision meshes, retained exactly

authoredInterpretation.doorPlacement: Authored axes moved 2.2 m east from the prior x28/42 positions to keep the retained canopy columns outside the door landings. Nearest column clears the 2.9 m opening edge by 0.58 m and the 3.2 m landing edge by 0.43 m. Neither axis is claimed to be a measured as-built main entrance.
authoredInterpretation.details: Glazing subdivisions, transom height, frame dimensions and threshold geometry are restrained authored approximations, not survey dimensions. Opaque backing closes the exterior; no invented lobby is supplied.
authoredInterpretation.paving: L-shaped infill closes only the 8.48 m western gap and 3.43 m eastern gap to the existing apron beginning local z=22.5. BU_PUBLIC_FRONTAGES omits custom CDS so no auto-frontage overlaps this infill. Paving is draped at terrain +0.039 m.
authoredInterpretation.landing: Two 3.2 m wide short approaches join the rigid +0.15 m sill top to the terrain apron. A 0.42 m deep level threshold prevents a suspended sill lip; ground outside this narrow approach remains unflattened.

validation.rays: Exterior glazing precedes backing on both exposed tower faces; double-door glass lies behind projecting jambs; visible geometry rays along both door centerlines and leaves reach the doors before any column; all approaches remain outside closed wall collision; ground heights follow DEM and meet door sills continuously.
